title: The Event
question: What does failed mean, and when did it happen?
goals: Learn the new columns, then load and look.
See why the flag cannot be a target.
Date the failure and build the label.
Test the label against the accounts.
Read the failure rate year by year.
Account for the companies that leave.
Draw survival curves that count every exit.
Compare labels at one, two, and three years.
Write the tables the next chapters read.

split.name: Testing on companies the model has met
split.naive_label: ROC-AUC, rows held out at random
split.why: Every row of a company carries the same flag, so a random split lets the model recognize it.

censoring.name: Treating every other exit as censoring
censoring.why: Kaplan-Meier describes a world where no company leaves another way, and {{ch2.cif_left_at:.0%}} do.
